newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton prices firm on lack of sellers.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton prices firm on lack of sellers.

text.p: Lack of origin sales offers boosted prices in the Bremen cotton market, a fortnightly market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said.

Consumers seeking spot West African and Central Asian grades found few original offers and had to buy expensive second hand material ex-trade, said the Exchange, which serves the European textile industry.
New crop markets were also quiet.

Among the sales reported by the Exchange were Central Asian standards 1, 2 and 3 as well as West African, Australian high and Indian medium grades, Syrian low to high grades, Greek high grades and Argentine cotton for a variety of 1997 and 1998 dates.

In long staples, the Exchange reported activity in Israel-Pima for second and third quarter 1997, U.S.-Pima for first half 1998 as well as some some nearby Egyptian Giza 75/85/86 and Giza 70/77 sales.
Cotton stocks as of June 20 totalled 43,018 bales, down from 103,130 bales a year earlier and compared with 39,120 bales a fortnight earlier.
